front.title: URI and QR Code Representations of PRP References

abstract.t: This document defines equivalent textual and binary carriers for a PRP reference followed by optional opaque application parameters. The textual form is the prp URI scheme with canonical unpadded base64url. The binary form is the same decoded payload without a textual prefix and is suitable for QR Code byte mode.

The carrier supports IDENTITY, ALIAS, MULTICAST and GROUPCAST references. It identifies a logical PRP object rather than a machine or network address and grants no authority merely by transporting it.

section.name: Introduction
section.t: Reference sharing needs a compact binary representation for byte-oriented transports and a canonical textual representation for URI-only systems. Both forms defined here carry the same payload and preserve any application parameter octets exactly.

Social contact sharing is one use, but it does not define this carrier. Any service can consume a shared reference. Public profile or service data can be obtained through the applicable authenticated protocol and need not be duplicated in the carrier.

section.name: Requirements Language
section.t: The key words MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD, SHOULD NOT, and MAY in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 when, and only when, they appear in all capitals.

section.name: Common Binary Payload
section.t: Both carriers encode one complete PRP reference followed by an optional application-owned byte string:
section.sourcecode:
P = reference || application_parameters
reference = reference_header:u8 || reference_suite:u16be || identifier:L
section.t: The reference header values are 0x00 IDENTITY, 0x01 ALIAS, 0x02 MULTICAST and 0x03 GROUPCAST. Bits 7 through 2 are reserved and MUST be zero. The recognized class/suite pair fixes L. The initial suites 0x0001, 0x0002, 0x0003 and 0x0005 use L=32; suite 0x0004 uses L=48. A parser MUST NOT infer L from remaining bytes. Unknown or unsupported class/suite pairs fail closed.

All four forms are PRP Self-Certifying Identifier References (SCIRs) defined by . Each class has distinct certifying material and does not inherit IDENTITY possession semantics. Every octet after the exact reference boundary is an opaque application parameter sequence, which can be empty. Parameters are not part of the reference and gain no authenticity or authority by proximity to it.

section.name: Binary Representation
section.t: The binary representation is exactly P without a prefix, character encoding, outer version, or length field. In a QR Code it is placed in byte mode. Its first octet is the reference header, not the ASCII letter “p”.

A byte-oriented API MUST NOT decode the binary form as text or apply character-set conversion. An application that accepts both forms must know whether its scanner or transport returned bytes or text.

section.name: Textual URI Representation
section.t: The textual form is:
ALPHA and DIGIT are defined by . The encoded-payload is the canonical unpadded base64url representation of P as defined in Section 5 of .

URI scheme matching is case-insensitive under . Producers MUST emit lowercase “prp:”. The encoded payload is case-sensitive. Padding, whitespace, ordinary base64 characters, authority, query, fragment, and relative forms are not defined and MUST be rejected.

An operating-system dispatch facility can match scheme strings more narrowly than the generic URI syntax. Direct parser acceptance of an uppercase scheme therefore does not prove platform dispatch. Producers use lowercase “prp:” for both canonical representation and dispatch interoperability; platform behavior requires separate validation.

A decoder MUST reject an encoded length congruent to one modulo four, nonzero unused final bits, and every noncanonical spelling. It can add padding internally for a base64url primitive but MUST reject “=” in the external form and verify equality with a canonical re-encoding.
The experimental spelling “prp:HH:<hex>”, including “prp:01:<hex>”, is not part of this scheme and MUST NOT be accepted through fallback or format guessing.

section.name: Processing and Equivalence

ol.li: distinguish binary input from a textual prp URI;
recover P exactly, decoding base64url once for the URI form;
parse and validate one complete reference using its assigned class and suite;
deliver the exact remaining octets to the selected application; and
apply the authority and resolution rules of that reference class.

section.t: Canonical equality of complete carrier values is equality of P. Reference equality compares only the parsed reference. Two values with the same reference and different application parameters identify the same PRP object while remaining different complete carrier values.

The safe default action for URI invocation is parsing and presentation. Invocation alone MUST NOT accept a contact, establish a session, publish information, grant authority, or perform another consequential action.

section.name: QR Code Mapping
section.t: The binary form is encoded in QR Code byte mode. The textual URI is also encoded in byte mode because the base64url alphabet is not confined to the QR alphanumeric alphabet. A PRP QR profile uses error-correction level H and includes a four-module quiet zone.

A QR profile MUST define a maximum presentation square, integral pixels per module, media and camera classes, distance, angle, focus, illumination, damage conditions, trial count, and scan-success threshold. It then selects the largest empirically qualified QR version. Resolution alone is not readability evidence.

Let C be the qualified byte-mode capacity at level H and R the complete reference length for the recognized class/suite pair. The binary parameter budget is C - R. For the textual form, the greatest decoded payload length is floor(3 * (C - 4) / 4), and the parameter budget is:

A common-domain profile should use the textual budget for both forms so that every admitted payload fits either representation at the same QR version. This document does not assign a universal QR version or byte maximum; those values require the empirical profile.

section.name: Input Limits
section.t: Implementations MUST enforce a documented finite input bound before decoding or allocating a decoded buffer, and a finite decoded payload bound before parsing or copying parameters. A URI implementation limit is local policy unless a consuming profile defines a smaller interoperable maximum. QR profiles necessarily impose their qualified capacity. A producer MUST NOT claim protocol-wide QR readability from theoretical symbology capacity alone.

ul.li: A valid carrier does not authenticate its publisher or prove that a displayed reference is the one intended by a user.
An attacker can replace an entire QR Code with another valid value.
Applications must validate opaque parameters in their own context.
Stable references permit correlation across applications and time.
Private keys, session secrets, and private profile data must not be placed in either representation.
Parsers must reject noncanonical encodings, bound allocation, and avoid repeated decoding or implicit character conversion.

section.name: IANA Considerations
section.t: IANA is requested to register the “prp” scheme in the URI Schemes registry. During Internet-Draft development the author can request a Provisional registration under . Publication on the Standards Track requests transition to Permanent status with the IETF as change controller.

section.name: Exact Carrier Vectors
section.t: These vectors use illustrative suite 0x0005 references whose 32-octet identifier is the sequence 00 through 1f. They test carrier conversion and class dispatch only and assert no class-specific authority proof.
